components.name: Flag Button
components.description: The single primary action: orange and white diagonal split with ink label.
components.css: .ds-flag { position: relative; height: 64px; width: 320px; border: 2px solid #111111; border-radius: 2px; background: linear-gradient(to bottom right, #F26B1D 0%, #F26B1D 50%, #FFFFFF 50%, #FFFFFF 100%); color: #111111; font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 26px; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; } .ds-flag:hover { filter: brightness(0.95); } .ds-flag:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #111111; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-flag:active { filter: brightness(0.88); }

components.name: Rule Button
components.description: Secondary action: 2 dp ink box, no fill.
components.css: .ds-rule-btn { min-height: 48px; padding: 8px 16px; border: 2px solid #111111; border-radius: 2px; background: transparent; color: #111111; font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 17px; letter-spacing: 0.8px; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; } .ds-rule-btn:hover { background: #F1F1F1; } .ds-rule-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #111111; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-rule-btn:active { background: #D9D9D9; }

narrative.overview: Every walk is an orienteering Score-O course. The app is the paper you are handed at the start: a control description sheet, a map with overprint, and at the end a punch card. It is white, ruled in hard ink, and almost entirely monochrome, so that the two colors it does own carry meaning. Material 3 supplies structure; the brand lives in the theme layer on top of it.
keyCharacteristics: Pure white paper and ink #111111; never cream.
Color is quarantined: purple is overprint and control numbers, orange is the flag and the one primary action.
Hard 2 dp rules form the grid; corners are 2 dp.
Barlow Condensed for sheet voice, the system face for story text.
Night-O theme follows the system: white rules on black, lighter purple.

rules.name: The Quarantine Rule
rules.body: Purple belongs to overprint and control numbers. Orange belongs to the flag mark and the single primary action. Any other use of either is a defect.

rules.name: The Two-Value Pocket Rule
rules.body: On the run screen there is black, white, and nothing between: no grey, no accent.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Control numbers, minutes, timers and scores use tabular figures so they never jitter.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed speaks for the sheet; Roboto speaks for the story.

rules.name: The Flat-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Surfaces stay flat at rest and under touch. Separate with a rule, not a shadow.

dos: Do separate content with 2 dp ink rules and keep corners at 2 dp.
Do reserve orange for the flag button and the "H" hint mark, and purple for overprint and control numbers.
Do use Barlow Condensed uppercase for headings and labels, tabular figures for any number, and Roboto for story text.
Do keep every touch target at 48 dp or more, and the flag button at 64 dp.
Do keep the run screen strictly black and white.
Do resolve colors through the theme roles so night-O comes along for free.
donts: Don't add shadows, elevation, gradients, or rounded cards.
Don't introduce cream or tinted paper; the sheet is pure white.
Don't use orange or purple as general accents, links, or decoration.
Don't place Give up next to Hint.
Don't fall back to the generic category layout: a full-bleed map with a bottom sheet and pins.
